doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: Soloing on 'Perdido' and the $18 pay
summary: He faked the solo from the melody's outline, played with that band for years, and was paid about $18.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Okay take me back to “Perdido” because I’m curious as after you played the melody did the band leader say, “Okay you got it.”

No he said, “Can you play a solo?” And I said, “Well if somebody else plays first.” Because the wheels were turning for me, right? You know? And I don’t know why but they were — I said well I’m going to figure out. So I heard it and I said, “Wait, I can play that, that’s in C, the beginning of it.” You know? Oh yeah, this middle section’s got some different chords in it. But it’s got some Es in it. So you see what I mean? So I was playing like the outline. But it was great. And I played with that band for years. I played with these musicians, and they would play with different groups, and I imagine they must have said, “Well look at this young guy, he can play pretty well and he knows the songs.” See so I could play the melody even if it wasn’t — because every day I’d learn a couple of tunes. I’d transpose them because I said if I get called to do something now I’ve got to know the tunes.
But just so we have this story complete, do you recall what you were paid for that first —
Oh yeah, it was about $18. 18. It was under $20 I remember that.
I’ll bet it was more than you were getting on the paper route. Say that again?

I felt like a millionaire. Because my friends were working at McDonald’s for $1.25 an hour. They were working all week and I made more money than they did just playing for two, three hours. Sometimes four. But you know I did sometimes two things on a weekend. So my little sister, she’s 14 years younger than me, I could buy stuff for her, I’d go to the fish store and get some good fish for — my mom loved fish and I love fish. My dad never was a big fish person. Anyway, even when I came home from college, I never
went home first. I went to the fish store. And when I pulled in the driveway the first thing I did was take the fish in. You know what I mean?
